articles.title: Building a Referral Engine in B2B Services
articles.excerpt: Ask almost any leader of a professional services firm where their best clients come from, and you will hear some version of the same answer: referrals. Referred clients tend to trust you faster, negot…
articles.body: Ask almost any leader of a professional services firm where their best clients come from, and you will hear some version of the same answer: referrals. Referred clients tend to trust you faster, negotiate less aggressively and stay longer. Yet most firms treat referrals as luck. They are grateful when one arrives and do little to make the next one more likely. Over the years, both as a partner in a software consulting company that grew rapidly and as the founder of a fully remote consultancy, I learned that referrals can be engineered. Not manipulated, but deliberately cultivated. A referral engine is a set of habits and systems that make it easy and natural for satisfied people to send good business your way. Here is how I think about building one.

articles.title: Threading and Code Execution in Rails: Executor, Reloader, and Load Interlock
articles.excerpt: Rails handles concurrency for us in many situations. But what happens when we create our own threads? How does Rails safely reload application code while other threads are running? And what does the E…
articles.body: Rails handles concurrency for us in many situations. But what happens when we create our own threads? How does Rails safely reload application code while other threads are running? And what does the Executor have to do with database connections and autoloading? I recently explored these questions while reading the Rails 8 guides. Here are my notes, with examples to make the concepts easier to understand. 1. How Rails Handles Concurrency Rails allows different operations to run concurrently. For example, when using a threaded web server such as Puma, multiple HTTP requests can be processed simultaneously. Active Job can also execute multiple jobs concurrently, depending on the queue adapter and its configuration. Action Cable handles messages using threads as well.

articles.title: Hunting for NSD exploitation attempts instead of waiting for an alert
articles.excerpt: Hunting for NSD exploitation attempts instead of waiting for an alert No public exploit has been reported for the four NSD stack overwrite flaws fixed in 4.15.3, and SecurityOnline records no confirme…
articles.body: Hunting for NSD exploitation attempts instead of waiting for an alert No public exploit has been reported for the four NSD stack overwrite flaws fixed in 4.15.3, and SecurityOnline records no confirmed in-the-wild use. That absence is a reason to build detection before the code appears, not a reason to relax. The flaws sit in the zone-file parser, which means the interesting events happen around zone loading rather than around DNS queries. What the vulnerabilities require NLnet Labs lists CVE-2026-101338, CVE-2026-101339, CVE-2026-101341 and CVE-2026-101337 as stack overwrites in NSD 4.10.0 through 4.15.2. Each requires a crafted zone file fed directly to the parser.

articles.title: "Film look" is a contrast curve, not a noise stamp — what style presets actually change
articles.excerpt: "Make it look like film" sounds like a texture request. It is really four separate changes to how your pixels behave, and the difference between applying them and just stamping noise on top is the dif…
articles.body: "Make it look like film" sounds like a texture request. It is really four separate changes to how your pixels behave, and the difference between applying them and just stamping noise on top is the difference between a photo that reads as scanned film and a photo that reads as a filtered phone shot. Here is what actually changes, and how to tell what a tool did. The four components of a film look Grain sits in the midtones, not everywhere. Organic film grain is strongest in the middle values and nearly invisible in deep shadows and blown highlights, because it is an artifact of dye clouds, not an overlay. A noise layer applied uniformly at a fixed opacity is the single most recognizable tell of a fake: grain over jet-black areas does not happen on real film.

articles.excerpt: A support lead opens the inbox on Monday. A shopper asked the bot for a person on Saturday, but the chat is marked answered and nobody owns the next reply. How can you add human escalation to a chatbo…
articles.body: A support lead opens the inbox on Monday. A shopper asked the bot for a person on Saturday, but the chat is marked answered and nobody owns the next reply. How can you add human escalation to a chatbot? Give the shopper a reliable way to ask for a person, send the whole conversation to an owned queue, and say clearly when that person will respond. The transfer needs more than a polite closing sentence. In our sample HoverBot workspace, the inbox shows who is handling a conversation, who is viewing it, and an assignment control. The workspace and teammates pictured here are fictional. The useful design question is whether a support lead can see an unfinished handoff and put a name beside it before the customer asks again. Sample workspace with fictional teammates.

articles.title: Rubin telescope should find more of Earth's mysterious 'mini-moons' — including some we can study up close
articles.excerpt: Earth’s tiny, temporary moons could become some of the easiest asteroid targets for future missions. And we'll likely find more of them soon, thanks to the Rubin telescope.
articles.body: Earth almost always has more than one moon. The others are just very small, and they never stay long — but they could provide accessible and unique insights into the solar system. Temporary satellites, or mini-moons , are small asteroids that wander into Earth’s neighborhood and get captured briefly by our planet’s gravity. A typical one stays about nine months and circles Earth roughly three times before escaping back into orbit around the sun , Grigori Fedorets of Finland's University of Helsinki said in a presentation at the Europlanet Science Congress (EPSC) 2026 in The Hague in September. Fedorets' modeling suggests that the largest mini-moon around Earth at any given moment is typically only about 75 centimeters (30 inches) across.

articles.body: The full "Hunter's Moon" wowed stargazers with a breathtaking display of natural light when it rose to dominate the autumn sky overnight on Oct. 25-26. Here are our favorite photos captured from around the world. October's full moon is often known as the Hunter's Moon because it traditionally rose around the time that hunters would take to the newly harvested fields to catch animals to prepare as food for the coming winter. Well, in 2026 the Hunter's Moon certainly succeeded in captivating the imagination and attention of photographers, who snapped the lunar disk alongside magnificent natural vistas, glowing cityscapes and ancient wonders. Read on to enjoy the most spectacular images of the Hunter's Moon.
articles.author: Anthony Wood

articles.title: 'More missions, more often': NASA is overhauling how it selects science missions
articles.excerpt: NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster.
articles.body: NASA is overhauling how it selects and develops science missions, with changes intended to reduce costs, streamline competition and get missions into space faster. The new approach, called Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), was announced on Oct. 21 in an open letter from Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate (SMD), to the NASA science community. The changes, directed by NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, could significantly reshape how scientists, universities, NASA centers and commercial companies vie for future missions. "We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long," Fox stated in the letter.

M42: The Great Nebula in Orion Explanation: The Great Nebula in Orion , an immense, nearby starbirth region , is one of the most famous of all astronomical nebulas . Here, glowing gas surrounds hot young stars at the edge of an immense interstellar molecular cloud only 1500 light-years away.
